title: Dynamic geo capacity hints and quantile-driven steering
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Implement a new routing policy that incorporates per-region capacity hints, observed latency quantiles, and configurable geo-pinning fallbacks. Goal is to reduce cross-region latency spikes, avoid saturating limited dedicated pools, and provide deterministic shedding/circuit-breaker behaviour when regional capacity degrades.
motivation: Existing steering is static and frequently over-routes to under-provisioned regions during traffic spikes. That causes SLO violations and noisy failovers. By baking runtime capacity hints and 95th/99th quantile latency signals into routing decisions, we can make failover graceful and preserve priority traffic paths.
design_summary: Policy will score candidate regions per-request using: (1) configured geo_affinity weight, (2) real-time capacity_hint (free_slots / expected_qps) published by regional allocator, (3) recent observed p95 and p99 tail latency windows, and (4) explicit customer geo_pin tags. Score formula is tunable and evaluated in the steering controller. Circuit-breaker thresholds and shedding tiers are derived from the score band and SLO budget consumption.
acceptance_criteria: Routing controller exposes a new policy type 'dynamic_geo_capacity' in the config API
Per-region capacity_hint metric is published at 1s resolution and consumed by the controller
Controller uses p95/p99 latency windows (60s rolling) to de-prioritize regions exceeding thresholds
Circuit breaker triggers per-region with at least two configurable levels: soft (reject low-priority routes) and hard (reject all non-pinned routes)
End-to-end load test shows median cross-region failover time < 2s and end-to-end p99 latency improvement of 20% for affected customers versus baseline
Feature rollout gated by canary flag and telemetry that surfaces routing-induced SLOs in Console
implementation_steps: Add capacity_hint metric to regional allocator and ensure it is emitted to the global control plane
Implement score engine in steering controller with plugin points for different quantiles and weights
Add customer-facing geo_pin attribute on routes and implement pin-respect logic in controller
Implement circuit breaker policy that uses score bands and SLO budget to decide soft/hard shedding
Create e2e tests: synthetic multi-region traffic, simulated capacity exhaustion, and graceful shedding validation
Instrument metrics and Console dashboards: routes affected, re-routes/sec, p95/p99 per-route, circuit-breaker activations
testing_plan: Unit tests for score computation with deterministic inputs
Integration tests between allocator -> controller -> proxy using local test harness
Chaos job: progressively reduce capacity_hint in a region and verify steering behavior
Load test with mix of pinned/unpinned routes to validate shedding tiers and SLO preservation
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in a staging region with monitoring alerts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy capacity_hint signals causing oscillations. Mitigation: add smoothing and hysteresis windows and require consecutive breaches before re-routing.
Risk: mis-scored customer routes due to stale metrics. Mitigation: fall back to geo_pin and configured preferences when metrics are older than threshold.
Risk: customer confusion when pinned routes are rejected under hard break. Mitigation: document behavior and allow route-level SLA exemptions.
Risk: increased controller CPU for scoring. Mitigation: cache scores per-tenant-traffic-shard and evaluate at configurable sampling rate.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal e2e and staging canary (1 region, 5% traffic)
Stage 2: Gradual enable for low-risk customers (10-20%) with monitoring
Stage 3: Broader rollout after two weeks and zero critical regressions
Rollback: disable runtime flag and manually re-route pinned traffic if needed
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with allocator, runtime, and console owners. Agreed on capacity_hint schema and metric cadence.
2025-02-18: Prototype score engine implemented behind feature flag; initial p95-based de-prioritization works in local harness.
2025-02-24: Added smoothing and 3-sample hysteresis to prevent oscillation after early test failures.
2025-03-02: Integration tests green; preparing canary load test in staging for 2025-03-05. Created console dashboard mockups and alert rules.
notes: Decision: use p95 and p99 windows of 60s by default but make them configurable per-customer.
Decision: circuit breaker levels mapped to route priority; system will never shed 'critical' priority routes unless manually configured.
Follow-up: open a small ticket to add an API for customers to opt routes into 'priority-preserve' mode that bypasses soft shedding.
